reviewer_notes: Factually the S2 ideals are mostly sound: every evidence row picks the option its evidence supports, stays inside the stated budget, cites both records, names a trade-off and avoids guarantees. Every number and difference was re-checked (e.g. A048 0.2kg = 1.35-1.15, A046 £20 = 630-610, A029 ₹57,000 > ₹52,000): no arithmetic errors. The problems are structural and worse than S1. (1) 23/23 evidence rows use one template: exactly 2 options, 1 record each, and an option that plainly fails the stated need (no close calls, no 3-4 options, no NO-MATCH, no 'cheaper is right' except A043/A047). (2) S2 is supposed to carry UC1 (one laptop in hand) and UC2 (claim-by-claim pitch checks), but there are 0 single-laptop second opinions and 0 pitch rows with 3+ claims; A033 and A042 touch a single seller claim only. (3) Evidence never states n ('each may summarize one or more reports'), so calibration can't be graded. (4) Product names collide inside S2 with different specs (Fast15 A027/A030, Route14 A031/A048, Ledger15 A032/A046, Arena15 A030/A044, Canvas16/Canvas14-P/E) and across scenarios (Comet14/Forge15 = A001; Learn14 = A013): a split by row leaks. (5) Only 1 Hinglish row (A036), 0 te-en/ta-en, 1 non-India row (A046, GBP). (6) Next steps are almost always a generic 'verify X before buying'; no row uses F3, F5, F6 or F7 even where the query asks for a check (A041) or a cost decision (A029). (7) All 146 assertions are semantic; the budget ceiling, 'uses both citations' and question count are deterministic. A026.5 asks for a next check about 'four years of battery life', which the query never raises.

rows.proposed_ideal: The seller's 'both upgradeable' is true for only one of them. Stack14-16 (₹64,000): ✓ two RAM slots and 32GB support in the spec, and a reviewer installed 2×16GB and finished the CAD exercise, though opening the case needed care [A033-R1]. Because that reviewer fitted two 16GB sticks, plan on possibly replacing the factory memory, not just adding to it. Stack14-8 (₹59,000): ≠ 8GB is soldered with no slot, and an owner confirmed this after buying despite the seller's claim [A033-R2]. For 32GB later, take Stack14-16. Next step: ask the seller whether the 16GB is one stick or two, and check the warranty terms on opening the case.
